title: Release Manifest
description:
An immutable, versioned description of one shipment.

Immutability is the point. Once frozen at RC, a release manifest never changes — any correction produces a new release. That is what makes rollback possible as an operation rather than a rebuild: rolling back means re-publishing a previous manifest, which only works if manifests are retained and trustworthy.

Target platforms carry their role (required/optional) HERE rather than in the strategy, because which platforms must succeed is a per-release policy: r1 may ship Yandex-only and r2 may add CrazyGames.

Since 1.1.0 a manifest the Factory drafts also says what it rests on: the qa-report and verification-report it was cleared by, the commit every upstream report named, the evidence status per platform (PASS_MOCK and BLOCKED_EXTERNAL are carried as such, never upgraded), the audit of every package, the template revision, and the workflow run that produced it. All of it is optional, so a 1.0.0 manifest written by a game repository's own tooling still validates.

packages.description: One per targeted platform. Built artifacts differ per platform because each profile shapes the bundle.

content_digest.description: Since 1.1.0. sha256 over the archive's entry names and the sha256 of each entry's bytes, in name order. Unlike `checksum` it does not change with file timestamps or compression, so it identifies what ships even when the archive bytes are not reproducible.

role.description: The release is LIVE only when every required platform is live; otherwise PARTIALLY_LIVE. Publication is not atomic — portals moderate independently.

profile_version.description: Pinned, so the build stays reproducible against the compliance rules in force when it shipped.

store_metadata.description: Per-platform submission material. Completeness of this is the guard on G6 — a missing required locale is the classic late failure.

rollback_target_release_id.description: The known-good manifest to re-publish. Named in advance, at G6, rather than found under pressure.

workflow.description: Since 1.1.0. The Factory workflow run and step execution that drafted this manifest.

template.description: Since 1.1.0. The web-game-template revision the game was generated from, and where the version was read.

source.description: Where `version` came from: a template marker, the inherited CHANGELOG, or package.json.

evidence.description: Since 1.1.0. What this release was cleared by. A draft is only produced from a passing qa-report of the newest verification, whose commit every upstream report and the checkout share.

status.description: The verification's own evidence status. PASS_MOCK when anything required was observed only against a stand-in.

commit_lineage.description: Every commit named by the evidence and the checkout. The verified commit (qa-report, verification-report, sdk-report, checkout) is one; since 1.2.0 `sdk-report.base` and `prototype-report` name the commit develop made, which sdk built on. The commit lineage rule (docs/core-contracts.md) holds between them, or there is no manifest.

source.description: An artifact type, or `checkout` for the repository's HEAD.

bundle_hash.description: The digest of the built bundle that was verified and then packaged: the verification-report's build_artifact.content_hash, recomputed from the checkout before packaging.

package_audit.description: What every package was checked for before this manifest was written. A draft exists only when every rule held.

source_manifest_hash.description: content_hash of the manifest the game repository's own tooling wrote, which this one extends.

review.description: Since 1.2.0. The independent review of the commit develop made, as the run holds it. `approved`: a review-report approved exactly the prototype-report's commit. `skipped`: no reviewer was configured, so the build is UNREVIEWED - this is never an approval. `absent`: the run holds no review-report. A request for changes, or an approval of another commit, produces no manifest.
